title: Kummer computation on a proper curve
statement:
Let $k$ be algebraically closed, let $C$ be a
smooth proper connected curve of genus $g$ over
$k$, and let $n\geq1$ be prime to $\operatorname{char}k$.
Then, under the canonical trivialization
$\theta_\zeta$ for a primitive root $\zeta$
([def-sc-mu-trivialization], existence by
[lem-sc-primitive-root]), the constant sheaf
$\mathbf F_n$ satisfies

$$
H^0(C_{\Et},\mathbf F_n)\cong\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z,\qquad
H^1(C_{\Et},\mathbf F_n)\cong(\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z)^{2g},\qquad
H^2(C_{\Et},\mathbf F_n)\cong\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z,
$$

and $H^q(C_{\Et},\mathbf F_n)=0$ for $q>2$.

proof.text: Choose a primitive $n$-th root $\zeta$ by [lem-sc-primitive-root]. The isomorphism of etale sheaves $\theta_\zeta:\mathbf F_n\xrightarrow{\sim}\mu_n$ of [def-sc-mu-trivialization] induces isomorphisms $H^q(C_{\Et},\mathbf F_n)\cong H^q(C_{\Et},\mu_n)$ in every degree. The choice of $\zeta$ is why these identifications are noncanonical.

source.place: Lemma Tag 03RQ, label lemma-cohomology-smooth-projective-curve, final paragraph

proof.text: The smooth curve $C$ is reduced. Its properness and connectedness meet the final specialization in [lem-sc-kummer-les]: $\mathcal O_C(C)^\times=k^\times$ and the $n$-th power map on this group is surjective because $k$ is algebraically closed. Also $H^2(C_{\Et},\mathbf G_m)=0$ by [lem-sc-brauer-zero]. Apply the exact Kummer cohomology sequence of [lem-sc-kummer-les], under these hypotheses, to get $H^1(C_{\Et},\mu_n)\cong\operatorname{Pic}(C)[n]$ and $H^2(C_{\Et},\mu_n)\cong\operatorname{coker}(n:\operatorname{Pic}(C)\to\operatorname{Pic}(C))$. Its degree-zero clause and [lem-sc-primitive-root] give $H^0(C_{\Et},\mu_n)\cong\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 03RQ, label lemma-cohomology-smooth-projective-curve, proof, first paragraph and Kummer long exact sequence

proof.text: For this smooth proper connected curve and $n$ invertible in $k$, [lem-sc-pic-proper-ntorsion] identifies $\operatorname{Pic}(C)[n]\cong(\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z)^{2g}$ and $\operatorname{coker}(n:\operatorname{Pic}(C)\to\operatorname{Pic}(C))\cong\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z$. Substitute these in the degree-one and degree-two identifications of step 2, then use the sheaf isomorphism of step 1 to obtain the three asserted groups for $\mathbf F_n$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 03RQ, label lemma-cohomology-smooth-projective-curve, proof, degree diagram and final paragraph

proof.text: The constant sheaf $\mathbf F_n$ is torsion, and $C$ is smooth, separated and connected of dimension one by [def-sc-curves]. Hence [lem-sc-cohomological-dimension] applies and gives $H^q(C_{\Et},\mathbf F_n)=0$ for every $q>2$.
